summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes and bilateral below-knee amputations was admitted after her visiting nurse noted a small erosion with exposed bone on her right amputation site. She denied pain, fever, or systemic symptoms and had been recently discharged two days prior for a brief episode of vomiting. Examination revealed a 0.5 cm area of serous drainage over the tibial tuberosity without erythema or purulence. Laboratory results showed mild leukocytosis and elevated glucose. She was treated with IV antibiotics and wound care. Surgery was recommended to cover the exposed bone, but the patient declined immediate intervention and planned to return the following week. She was discharged home with nursing support, oral Bactrim for 14 days, and instructions to monitor for signs of infection. Follow-up was arranged for surgical evaluation.
